title: Your Multimodal Speech Model Says I Have a Face for Radio
abstract: arXiv:2605.30472v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As large neural models have become better at language tasks, researchers are increasingly building multi- and omnimodal models that handle more than one modality of data. One example is the expansion of speech recognition models to audio-visual data, the goal being noise mitigation and multimodal subtitling. While performance and bias have been studied extensively in the single-modality regime, it is unknown how new modalities affect this, even though they produce biases in humans. We therefore propose the first bias evaluation of multimodal speech recognition, where we create videos pairing different faces with the same audio using lip-sync, and measure changes in speech transcription accuracy. We find large quality-of-service differences across mWhisper-Flamingo and Gemini models, with drops of up to 4.05 word error rate points, across self-declared gender, ethnicity, and their intersection. translated_title: 你的多模态语音模型说我长了一张“只适合上广播的脸”
translated_abstract: 随着大型神经网络模型在语言任务上的表现不断提升，研究人员正越来越多地构建能够处理多种数据模态的多模态和全模态模型。一个例子是将语音识别模型扩展到视听数据，其目标是降噪和多模态字幕生成。尽管在单模态场景下性能与偏见已被广泛研究，但新模态如何影响这些方面尚不清楚，即使这些新模态会在人类中引发偏见。因此，我们提出了首个针对多模态语音识别的偏见评估：我们利用唇形同步技术创建将不同面孔与相同音频配对的视频，并测量语音转录准确率的变化。我们发现mWhisper-Flamingo和Gemini模型在服务质量上存在巨大差异，在自我声明性别、种族及其交叉类别上，词错误率最多上升4.05个百分点。我们的研究结果为开发（工作）指明了优先事项。
tldr: 首次对多模态语音识别进行了偏见评估，发现当不同面孔与相同音频配对时，mWhisper-Flamingo和Gemini模型的词错误率最多上升4.05个百分点，揭示了基于性别、种族及其交叉类别的显著服务质量差异。
en_tdlr: First bias evaluation of multimodal speech recognition reveals that pairing different faces with the same audio causes word error rate increases of up to 4.05 points across self-declared gender, ethnicity, and their intersection in mWhisper-Flamingo and Gemini models.
